name: gnirehtet
why: Reverse tethering that routes an Android phone's network through adb, a clever hack on USB networking.

brief.what_it_is: Gnirehtet is a command-line tool that gives an Android phone the internet connection of the computer it is plugged into over USB, a setup the README calls reverse tethering. It takes the phone's traffic, relays it through adb to a relay server on the computer, and sends it out through the computer's network. It needs no root on either the device or the computer, and runs on GNU/Linux, Windows and macOS. It relays TCP and UDP over IPv4 only; IPv6 is not supported. The Android side is a small APK that the tool installs, and the app has no UI of its own.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as a way for devices to use the internet connection of the computer they are plugged into, without root access. The name is the word tethering reversed, and the project's own joke is "rev <<< tethering" (in Bash).
brief.how_it_works: The computer runs a relay server (Rust or Java) and sets up an adb reverse tunnel, adb reverse localabstract:gnirehtet tcp:31416, to the phone. A small APK on the phone is started with an adb shell command and forwards the phone's TCP and UDP traffic through that tunnel to the relay, which passes it to the computer's network. The README does not go into further detail about the protocol.

commands_seen.context: Homebrew install of the Rust flavor, per the README's Get the app section.
Turns on reverse tethering for exactly one device; stays active until Ctrl+C. On Windows, replace ./gnirehtet with gnirehtet.
Enables reverse tethering for all connected devices, present and future.
Starts the relay server and keeps it open, for the split-step workflow.
Installs the gnirehtet APK on the Android device. The serial is only needed when adb devices lists more than one device.
Starts a client for one device, run in another terminal after relay.
Stops the client for one device.
Resets the tunnel, for when a device is unplugged and replugged while gnirehtet is active.
Manual route: installs the APK directly with adb instead of using the gnirehtet wrapper.

Manual route: sets up the adb reverse tunnel that the phone-side app connects through. The README then starts the client with adb shell am start, but that is a long multi-line command, so it is not reproduced here.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew gives the Rust flavor (brew install gnirehtet). The Brew caveats say adb must be on PATH at runtime and suggest brew install --cask android-platform-tools. Enable adb debugging on each device. The Android app needs API 21 (Android 5.0) or later. The Java flavor needs Java 8 (JRE); on Debian-based distros the README names openjdk-8-jre. On Windows, if adb is only for this tool, the README says to copy adb.exe, AdbWinApi.dll and AdbWinUsbApi.dll into the gnirehtet directory. Other options: the ADB environment variable sets a custom adb path, and GNIREHTET_APK sets a custom APK path. On first run, the phone shows a permission popup, and a key icon appears in the status bar while the tunnel is active. The README also lists SHA-256 checksums for the release archives.
brief.standout: The phone needs no root and no special driver. It only needs adb, which the developer tooling already uses, and the entire tunnel is built on adb reverse. The project has two implementations: a Rust build that the README recommends, and a Java build that works anywhere Java 8 runs.
brief.status: Explicitly not actively maintained. The README says: "This project is not actively maintained anymore, only major blockers (like build issues) are fixed. It should still work, though." The current release is v2.5.1 (Rust and Java). The macOS Rust build is still v2.2.1, which the README marks as an old release. I did not see a release date or last commit date in the README.
brief.caveats: Maintenance has stopped, so only build-breaking issues get fixes. IPv6 is not supported. The macOS Rust download is the older v2.2.1 build. The Java flavor requires Java 8. The Android app requires API 21 or later. adb must be on PATH or pointed to with ADB, and adb debugging must be enabled on the device. The tool needs the phone to have USB debugging enabled and to accept the permission popup on first run.
quotes: This project is not actively maintained anymore, only major blockers (like build issues) are fixed. It should still work, though.
The application has no UI, and is intended to be controlled from the computer only.

judge.reason: Reverse-tethering an Android phone through adb without root is a neat, non-obvious use of developer tooling that makes ordinary USB debugging do something surprising.

entry.title: gnirehtet
entry.tldr: Gives an Android phone your computer's internet connection over USB, tethering in reverse, with no root and no UI on the phone.
entry.deeper_look:
Gnirehtet is the word tethering spelled backwards, and the README's own joke is `rev <<< tethering`. Ordinary tethering shares a phone's connection with a computer. This does the opposite: a phone plugged in over USB uses the computer's network, with no root on either side.

The computer runs a relay server, written in Rust or Java. It sets up an adb reverse tunnel (`adb reverse localabstract:gnirehtet tcp:31416`) to the phone. A small APK the tool installs has no interface of its own. It captures the phone's TCP and UDP traffic and pushes it through that tunnel to the relay, which sends it out over the computer's connection. A key icon shows in the status bar while the tunnel is up.

The idea underneath is that adb is more than a debugging shell. Its port-forwarding features can carry a whole network stack's worth of traffic, and nothing special is needed on the phone besides the app. It is a small, readable example of tunneling and relaying packets, and it can help when a device has no Wi-Fi or you are on a restricted network.
entry.install:
brew install gnirehtet
# adb must be on your PATH at runtime:
brew install --cask android-platform-tools
# Needs an Android phone (Android 5.0 / API 21+) with USB debugging enabled, connected by USB.

try_this.what_happens: Installs the app if needed and turns on reverse tethering for one device. It stays active until you press Ctrl+C. Accept the permission popup on the phone the first time.
Enables reverse tethering for every connected device, now and in the future.
Lists the subcommands, including the relay, start, stop and tunnel steps for running things manually.

entry.whats_unique: It needs no root and no special driver, only adb, and the whole tunnel is built on `adb reverse`. It comes in two implementations: a Rust build the README recommends and a Java build for anywhere Java 8 runs.
entry.caveats: The README says the project is not actively maintained and only build blockers are fixed. It is IPv4 only, and the macOS Rust download is the older v2.2.1.
